title: Late-Night Soccer! England vs. Mexico Kicks Off at 1 a.m.
summary: Have you ever stayed up super late to watch a big game? Soccer fans in England are getting ready to do just that. Their team's World Cup match against Mexico kicks off at 1 a.m. on Monday morning! That's because the game is in Mexico City, where the time is different. At first, the match was almost moved to an earlier time, which would have made it start at noon in Mexico. But after a lot of back-and-forth, FIFA—the group that runs the World Cup—decided to keep the original late-night time. This upset some England fans who had already traveled to Mexico. One fan said he and his friends might have missed the game if it started earlier because their flights wouldn't land in time. He said the whole trip was very expensive and that FIFA didn't think about the fans. Back in the UK, the prime minister said pubs can stay open until 5 a.m. so fans can watch together. That's really unusual! More than 600 pubs owned by one company, Greene King, will be open late. So whether you're in Mexico or England, it's going to be a very late—or very early—night of soccer.
why_it_matters: When big events happen across time zones, it can mean staying up late, but it also shows why organizations should think about fans' travel plans.

background_read: Soccer, called football in most of the world, is the planet's most popular sport. The FIFA World Cup is a tournament held every four years, and this year Mexico is hosting.
Because Mexico is in a different time zone, games that start in the evening there are shown in the early hours of the morning in the United Kingdom.

Back in England, the government gave special permission for pubs to stay open late, and Greene King (a large British company that runs pubs) said over 600 of its locations will welcome fans until 5 a.m. so supporters can watch the match together.
Article_Structure: WHO: England's national soccer team, their fans, FIFA (the governing body), the UK prime minister, and Greene King (a pub company).
WHAT: The England vs. Mexico World Cup match kicks off at 1 a.m. UK time. British pubs have been allowed to stay open until 5 a.m. for fans to watch.
WHERE: The match is in Mexico City; fans in England will watch in pubs or at home.
WHY: The time difference means a night match in Mexico becomes very late in the UK. FIFA decided to keep the original time, though some traveling fans were unhappy because it disrupted their plans.

perspectives.description: They are excited to stay up late and watch the match together. The late opening hours turn it into a special community event.
They are upset because their expensive trips could have been wasted if the time changed. They feel FIFA didn't care about their plans.
They had to balance the needs of the host country's broadcast time, the players, and traveling fans. Keeping the original time avoided confusion but frustrated some supporters.
